reviews.lens: LANDO FIDELITY & ONE SYSTEM. I measured the page against the 12 laws and the census, using the review sheets, map.json, my own at-rest diffs every 450px (1440×900: full-res |Δ|≥4 and the census method, 360×225 >12), section and sticky geometry at 1440 and 390, and a live render of ?v=…+noc+apart.
reviews.verdict: The page is closer to one system than it has been, but it isn't there yet. What is now shared: one ground under every section (the field moves 0.8–2.9% at full res at almost every stop), one strip runner, small hovers everywhere, and one card-and-pill object that both the services and the work carry. What still reads as a collage: (1) There are TWO pinned horizontal rails, work at 43.7–62.6% and runs at 70.6–90.6%, and they use two different card skins. About 39% of the page scrolls sideways; Lando has one axis switch at 23.1%. (2) The testimonial tiles are the voices' three quotes, word for word, and they appear 3,500px apart. (3) The stretch Jake dislikes is three whitespace seams in a row (services exit → §02b → tiles → Proof), 1,100px of still centred text between the two loud pinned rooms. (4) At least five text motions play inside the reading zone: the masked rise, §02b's scrubbed sweep, the scrawl, the voices' blur focus-pull, and the close's line fill. Lando has one triggered wipe that finishes before you read. (5) There is no bookend. The close is the only left-set display type after the poster, and it has nothing moving at rest. On the census method, every stop from y 1800 to 13050 reads ≤0.13%. Pinned or stacked scroll is 67% of the page (9,000 of 13,411px); Lando's is 32%. Lando's grammar would make four moves here: cut to one horizontal scroll, the work rail Jake asked for; cut the duplicate tiles and move the promise to after the proof, so the statement → services → proof run is unbroken; flip the ground once, under that one rail; and close on a bookend that rhymes with the film and ticker. The ranked changes below build each of those as one trial.

The runs rail uses a different card (step cards with UI sketches), so 'the card' moves sideways in two different skins. Jake's own framing is 'OUR horizontal scroll for works': the runs rail dilutes it.

reviews.lens: One thing at a time (Jake's rule) and cognitive ease: how many focal points compete in each viewport, which beats repeat each other, and page length against what the page actually says. Evidence is the two review sheets plus 20 extra frames at 1440×900 and 8 at 390×844 (Playwright, script deleted afterwards). Each frame came with a count of the visible media and of type 36px or larger. No project files were edited.
reviews.verdict:
The page is 15.9 screens at 1440×900 (Lando's is 14.1), and about 3.3 of those screens say something the page has already said. 64% of the document sits under a pin or sticky: §02a 900 + services 2700 + work 2700 + runs 2862 = 9,162px. The hero, the held poster, each services card at rest, a rail card at the centre of its window, and the voices head at y 9000 all pass the one-focal test. y 9000 is the cleanest frame on the page. The failures cluster in four places:
(1) The same three quotes run twice: as tiles at y 5574, three at once, and again as the voices at 9069–10400.
(2) A second sideways rail, runs, is the single largest slice of the page (20%). It sits at 71–91%, shows three cards at once, has a near-empty frame at y 10250, and on the phone its head is printed on top of a voices quote.
(3) Desert Wings is on screen five times before the second case appears. The rail opens on the same 'WHERE PILOTS ARE BORN' screenshot that services card 1 showed 3,600px earlier.
(4) The stretch from y 4700 to 6100 (§02b, tiles, proof head) never gives a screen one job. At y 5000 there are eight targets: the sentence, four doors and three tiles. The four doors repeat the nav pill, which is on screen at the same moment.
Cutting the tiles and the runs, removing the doors, putting DW last in the rail and moving the ticker to the close brings the page to about 12.4 screens with one job per screen. None of this reverses the rail or the pin Jake loves.

That breaks Lando law 6 (no pins in the back 43%) and law 10 (switch axis once and give that switch the biggest budget). At rest it shows three step cards at once, so the eye has to choose. It also creates the page's deadest frame.

reviews.lens: The buyer's story and conversion. The visitor is an owner-run business (flight school, coach, clinic, contractor) who arrives from an ad. They need, in order: what is this, is it for me, show me it works, who is behind it, what does it cost, how does it go, how do I start.
reviews.verdict:
The first three screens do their job. The hero title and film say what this is (y 0). The audience ticker (y 1320) and the §02a poster holding the persona's word (y 1567) say who it's for, and Jake likes all three, so they stay. After that the story falls apart.

**Questions the page never answers:**
- **Who.** The rendered page never names Jake and never shows his face. "Built by the person you talk to." is a 43px clause at y ~5200.
- **Cost.** There is no price anywhere. "See your price →" is one of four equal ~13px text links at y 5420. "What does a website cost?" is an accordion at y 13370, 93% of the way down. The numbers are already written in lib/services.ts and never rendered: "From $2.5k · fixed quote in 2 days", "Quoted per project · no retainer", "$500/mo + your ad spend · no lock-in".

**Questions answered too much or too early:**
- **Proof is split into four places.** Services are three Desert Wings photos (y 2467). Placeholder tiles follow (y 5574), then the rail (y 6261), then voices (y 9069), which repeats the same three placeholder quotes word for word; the third reappears inside runs (y 10102).
- **"How it goes" gets 2,862px.** It is a second pinned sideways rail (runs), plus a 693px FAQ. Jake already decided on 09-19 to take both off the homepage; it hasn't been done.
- **The asks come too early and then stop.** §02b asks "Book the call" before any proof and splits the eye four ways. After the rail ends (y 8961) there is no door in the page for 4,800px (5.3 screens), until the close at y 13800.

**The fix is mostly subtraction plus two new jobs:**
- the price rides each service card's pill
- one "who" screen after the proof carries Jake, the how-it-goes line and one estimator door
- the tiles, §02b's four-link row, runs and objections come out

Every answer then lands one screen at a time in the buyer's order. The page drops from 14,311 to about 10,500px at 1440, and the pinned sideways work rail stays exactly as Jake asked for it.

synth.forJake:
The top of the page works: the title and film, the audience ticker, the held "Websites / Automation / Ads" screen, and the services one at a time. The new work rail works too. One big card per client, each with its pill, sliding sideways while the page holds. All three reviewers want to keep it exactly like that.

Three changes matter most:

1. Cut the three quote tiles. They repeat the same three quotes that show up again further down. They're also the one screen where the eye has three things to choose from.

2. Take the "how it runs" rail off the homepage. It's a second sideways scroll, so your work rail stops being the special one. You decided this on 09-19 and it never got done. It moves to the Services page.

3. Move the "Built by the person you talk to" sentence below the work and the quotes, and give it one button: See your price. Then the services run straight into your work, and most of the stretch you don't like goes away.

Together these make the page about a quarter shorter, with one thing to look at on every screen.

- A photo of you for that sentence. Right now the page never shows your face or your name.
- Real quotes from real clients, with names and their permission. The current ones are placeholders and can't go live.
- Your OK to show prices on the service cards. Nothing on the page says what anything costs yet.
